name: Paul Azinger
description: Pod system pioneer. Built complementary pairings with surgical precision. Your foursomes chemistry scores get a significant boost.
flavor_text: Azinger's 2008 Valhalla team is the gold standard of USA captaincy.

name: Steve Stricker
description: Data-driven and balanced. No single format dominates — every session gets a lift. Best when your roster is well-rounded.
flavor_text: Stricker's 2021 team won 19-9. Consistent excellence from wire to wire.

name: Davis Love III
description: Veteran leadership and belief. His teams fight hardest on Sunday. Big singles boost when your back is against the wall.
flavor_text: Led the USA comeback charge at Medinah. The 2012 team nearly pulled off the miracle.

name: Davis Love III
description: Second-time captain with lessons learned. More balanced approach, still relies on Sunday singles to close the deal.
flavor_text: Hazeltine 2016. Patrick Reed vs Rory McIlroy. USA won 17-11 in dominant fashion.

name: Jim Furyk
description: Steady, process-focused, pressure-resistant. Your team's composure is rewarded with a consistent boost across all formats.
flavor_text: The 2018 team fell short at Le Golf National but was never outclassed in spirit.

name: Zach Johnson
description: Faith and composure under pressure. Fourball specialist — his teams thrive in the aggressive, go-for-broke format.
flavor_text: Rome 2023. The wildcard selections defined his captaincy — high chemistry pairings key.

name: Hal Sutton
description: Bold pairings, high risk-reward. Famous for pairing Tiger and Phil together. Massive foursomes upside — but chemistry backfires can hurt.
flavor_text: Oakland Hills 2004 was a cautionary tale. Bold moves, catastrophic result. High variance captain.

name: Tom Lehman
description: Motivator and fourball specialist. His teams light up in the aggressive format. Great when your roster is full of birdie-hunters.
flavor_text: The 2006 team lost at The K Club but the fourball sessions were electric.

name: Seve Ballesteros
description: Pure fire. Maximum chemistry multiplier. The emotional engine of European golf. His fourball teams play inspired, creative, go-for-everything golf.
flavor_text: Seve at Valderrama — fists pumping, crowd roaring. The most electric captain in Ryder Cup history.

name: Sam Torrance
description: Builder of belief. His teams bond deeply and fight on Sunday. Consistent boosts across the board with emphasis on singles grit.
flavor_text: The Belfry 2002. Torrance masterminded a patient, clinical European win.

name: Bernhard Langer
description: Disciplined, methodical, pressure-resistant. Foursomes specialist who builds structured teams. High floor, low variance.
flavor_text: Oakland Hills 2004. 18.5-9.5. The most dominant European win in the modern era.

name: Bernhard Langer
description: Sage leadership returning to the big stage. More balanced than his 2004 version — experience has taught him every session matters equally.
flavor_text: Rome 2023. Langer brought calm authority to a new generation of European stars.

name: Ian Woosnam
description: Aggressive and birdie-focused. The highest fourball boost available. If your team likes to attack pins, Woosie unleashes them.
flavor_text: The K Club 2006. Darren Clarke played through grief. Europe won 18.5-9.5.

name: Nick Faldo
description: Analytical foursomes specialist. Six majors, six Ryder Cups played. Structures the team sheet like a chess grandmaster.
flavor_text: Valhalla 2008. Faldo's picks were controversial but his foursomes logic was sound.

name: Colin Montgomerie
description: Home crowd energy and singles fire. Monty was born for the Ryder Cup. His teams play Sunday like their lives depend on it.
flavor_text: Celtic Manor 2010. Three days of rain. Graeme McDowell holed the winning putt.

name: Jose Maria Olazabal
description: Heart, legacy, and Seve's spirit. Massive chemistry multiplier. His wildcard choices carry extra inspiration — the team fights for more than a trophy.
flavor_text: The Miracle at Medinah. Olazabal invoked Seve. Europe came back from 10-6 to win.

name: Paul McGinley
description: Tactical genius and master of pairing chemistry. Highest chemistry multiplier in the European pool. Your pairings will click in ways that surprise you.
flavor_text: Gleneagles 2014. McGinley's captaincy is studied in textbooks. Europe won comfortably.

name: Darren Clarke
description: Gritty, experienced, and links-hardened. Balanced across all formats. No weaknesses, no fireworks — just solid, dependable Ryder Cup craft.
flavor_text: Hazeltine 2016. Clarke's team was outgunned by USA's depth. Still fought to the end.

name: Thomas Bjorn
description: Detail-oriented and analytically balanced. Built the 2018 team around precision — the right format for Le Golf National. Excellent chemistry pairing instincts.
flavor_text: Le Golf National 2018. Molinari 5-0. Fleetwood iconic. Europe won 17.5-10.5.

name: Padraig Harrington
description: Experimental and fourball-heavy. Loves sending his bombers after birdies. If your team has attack dogs in fourball slots, Padraig amplifies them.
flavor_text: Whistling Straits 2021. Harrington's team was outclassed but fourball sessions were competitive.
